answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 for 30 days before it can submit ten bids per day, whether buying timber for a terrace or booking ocean freight. The quota is enforced against each bonded account, so creating names alone adds no bidding power. An attacker seeking 1,000 identities must immobilize $100,000 for a month, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital even if none of the accounts is caught misbehaving.
